correctness.rationale: The double has one vertex per original edge and one adjacency per pair of opposite edges in a boundary tetrahedron; no simplex of dimension at least two fits in a 3-dimensional boundary. An independent exact reconstruction at unit circumradius in Q(sqrt(5)) recovered all 600 tetrahedra by affine-rank and strict support tests, using the classical identification/count to ensure completeness. It gave 720 vertices, 1800 edges, degree 5 throughout, and one component. Removing each double edge in turn and taking the shortest alternate path gives girth 6, with a six-cycle witness. The supplied parent array was separately relabelled into this reconstruction and all 719 parent edges and root paths verified. The quotient map contracting a spanning tree is a homotopy equivalence to a wedge of 1800−720+1=1081 circles; no assertion that this quotient is literally an embedded retract is needed. The integral homology and fundamental group follow.
residual_risks: Only the standard convex {3,3,5} boundary and this doubling operation were audited; no symmetry-module or other-polytope conclusion follows.
